html.title: HTML Foundations
html.description: A practical beginner HTML course covering documents, text, links, images, lists, tables, semantic structure, forms, metadata, accessibility, and a complete single-page capstone.
html.moreComingSoon: More HTML Foundations lessons are coming soon.

html-module-1-first-web-pages.title: First Web Pages
html-module-1-first-web-pages.description: Build confidence with first web pages through visible browser-preview practice.
outcomes: Understand HTML as document structure that a browser parses and renders.
Build a page with doctype, html, head, title, and body.
Read opening tags, closing tags, nested content, and attributes.
why: Builds confidence with first web pages.
Prepares learners for the next skills in the course.

html-module-2-links-images-paths.title: Links, Images, and Paths
html-module-2-links-images-paths.description: Build confidence with links, images, and paths through visible browser-preview practice.
outcomes: Create links with anchor elements and useful link text.
Understand how URLs and local paths point to resources.
Add images with src and meaningful alt text.
why: Builds confidence with links, images, and paths.
Prepares learners for the next skills in the course.

html-module-3-lists-tables-content.title: Lists, Tables, and Structured Content
html-module-3-lists-tables-content.description: Build confidence with lists, tables, and structured content through visible browser-preview practice.
outcomes: Choose ordered or unordered lists based on content meaning.
Represent grouped and hierarchical information with nested lists.
Use table, caption, thead, tbody, tr, th, and td for tabular data.
why: Builds confidence with lists, tables, and structured content.
Prepares learners for the next skills in the course.

html-module-4-semantic-accessible-layout.title: Semantic and Accessible Page Structure
html-module-4-semantic-accessible-layout.description: Build confidence with semantic and accessible page structure through visible browser-preview practice.
outcomes: Use header, nav, main, and footer to describe major page regions.
Choose semantic content containers instead of generic wrappers when meaning exists.
Create a logical heading hierarchy and meaningful text alternatives.
why: Builds confidence with semantic and accessible page structure.
Prepares learners for the next skills in the course.

html-module-5-forms-inputs.title: Forms and User Input
html-module-5-forms-inputs.description: Build confidence with forms and user input through visible browser-preview practice.
outcomes: Connect labels to form controls and understand form structure.
Choose text, email, number, date, checkbox, radio, and other input types appropriately.
Collect longer text and choices with accessible controls.
why: Builds confidence with forms and user input.
Prepares learners for the next skills in the course.

html-module-6-final-capstone.title: Final Capstone: Personal Website
html-module-6-final-capstone.description: Bring the full HTML Foundations skill set together in one growing, cumulative, semantic, accessible multi-page website.
outcomes: Build one cumulative website whose files are introduced only when the project needs them.
Connect pages with meaningful navigation, relative links, and correctly referenced image assets.
Combine semantic structure, exact content, links, images, lists, tables, and a form appropriately.
Review document metadata, nesting, headings, labels, alt text, link text, and relative paths before submission.
Use the live browser preview and source validation to verify the complete final website.
why: Builds confidence with final capstone: personal website.
Prepares learners for the next skills in the course.
